From the text, BP=6, so write the moving point on the circle as P=(6 cos t, 6 sin t). Then compute PD=6 sqrt(9-4 cos t-4 sin t) and PC=6 sqrt(5-4 cos t). Hence the function is F(t)=6 sqrt(9-4 cos t-4 sin t)+3 sqrt(5-4 cos t). Differentiate: F'(t)=12(sin t-cos t)/sqrt(9-4 cos t-4 sin t)+6 sin t/sqrt(5-4 cos t). Set F'(t)=0 and solve together with cos^2 t+sin^2 t=1; the minimizing critical point satisfies 3 sin t=4 cos t-2, giving cos t=(8+3 sqrt 21)/25 and sin t=(4 sqrt 21-6)/25. Substituting into F gives sqrt(9-4 cos t-4 sin t)=(14-sqrt 21)/5 and sqrt(5-4 cos t)=(2 sqrt 21-3)/5, so F=6(14-sqrt 21)/5+3(2 sqrt 21-3)/5=15. Check the remaining critical/end cases around the circle give no smaller value, so the minimum is 15.

推理：按坐标法，取 B 为原点，BC 为 x 轴正方向，BA 为 y 轴正方向，则 C=(12,0)，D=(12,12)，A=(0,12)。因为 P 在以 B 为圆心、半径 6 的圆上，可设 P=(6cos t,6sin t)。

于是 PD=sqrt((12-6cos t)^2+(12-6sin t)^2)=6sqrt(9-4cos t-4sin t)，PC=sqrt((12-6cos t)^2+(0-6sin t)^2)=6sqrt(5-4cos t)。

令 F(t)=PD+1/2 PC=6sqrt(9-4cos t-4sin t)+3sqrt(5-4cos t)。

求导得 F'(t)=12(sin t-cos t)/sqrt(9-4cos t-4sin t)+6sin t/sqrt(5-4cos t)。令 F'(t)=0，并结合 cos^2 t+sin^2 t=1。按计算，最小值对应的临界点满足 3sin t=4cos t-2，因此 cos t=(8+3sqrt(21))/25，sin t=(4sqrt(21)-6)/25。

代入得 sqrt(9-4cos t-4sin t)=(14-sqrt(21))/5，sqrt(5-4cos t)=(2sqrt(21)-3)/5。所以 F=6(14-sqrt(21))/5+3(2sqrt(21)-3)/5=15。圆上一周的其余临界情形没有给出更小值，因此最小值为 15。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the side length of square $ABCD$ is $12$, and the radius of $\odot B$ is $6$. Point $P$ is a moving point on $\odot B$. What is the minimum value of $PD + \frac{1}{2}PC$?
raw_record.answer: Solution: Take $BE=3$ on $BC$ and connect $BP$ and $PE$. Since the side length of square $ABCD$ is $12$ and the radius of $\odot B$ is $6$, we have $BC=12=CD$, $BP=6$, and $EC=9$. Because $\frac{BP}{BC}=\frac{1}{2}=\frac{BE}{BP}$ and $\angle PBE=\angle PBC$, $\triangle PBE \sim \triangle CBP$. Therefore $\frac{BE}{BP}=\frac{PE}{PC}=\frac{1}{2}$, so $PE=\frac{1}{2}PC$. Hence $PD+\frac{1}{2}PC=PD+PE$. When points $D$, $P$, and $E$ are collinear, $PD+PE$ is minimized, so $PD+\frac{1}{2}PC$ is minimized. Therefore the minimum value is $DE=\sqrt{DC^2+CE^2}=\boxed{15}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there is a square ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right; a circle is drawn with B as the center, point P is on the circle, and in the figure the line segments from P to D and from P to C are connected. The problem statement gives that the side length of the square is 12, and the radius of circle B is 6, so BC=CD=12, BP=6.

Reasoning: According to the method, construct point E on BC such that BE=3, then EC=BC-BE=12-3=9, and connect PE. Because BE and BC are on the same straight line, ∠PBE=∠PBC. Also BP/BC=6/12=1/2, BE/BP=3/6=1/2, therefore from the included angle and the two sides being proportional, it can be obtained that △PBE∼△CBP. Thus the corresponding sides PE/PC=BE/BP=1/2, so PE=1/2 PC.

Therefore the original expression PD+1/2 PC=PD+PE. By the triangle inequality, PD+PE≥DE, and equality is attained when D, P, and E are three collinear points and P is on line segment DE. At this time the minimum value is DE. Because DC=12, CE=9, and DC⊥CE, DE=sqrt(12^2+9^2)=sqrt(144+81)=sqrt225=15.

So the minimum value is 15.
